newsitem.title: LATVIA: Latvia eyes EBRD, EIB interest in railway revamp.
newsitem.headline: Latvia eyes EBRD, EIB interest in railway revamp.

text.p: The European Bank for Reconstruction and Development (EBRD) may investment in Latvia's out-dated railways, and the country also hopes to interest the European Investment Bank (EIB), newspaper Dienas Bizness said on Friday.

It quoted Transport Minister Vilis Krishtopans as saying after meeting EBRD officials in London that the bank may help modernise important railway freight links from the start of 1998 and invest between $50 million and $60 million.
Krishtopans was also quoted as saying that he wanted to get the EIB more interested in Latvia.
"At the moment, there are no big projects with EIB participation and this lowers Latvia's rating," Krishtopans wsa quoted by Dienas Bizness as saying.
Latvia sees its railways as key in building a position as the best transit link between Russia and the West.
Krishtopans was in London as part of the delegation accompanying President Guntis Ulmanis on a visit to Britain.
The two sides also discussed the possibility of the EBRD investing in the $50 million to $60 million construction of a new passenger terminal at Riga airport.
Krishtopans also told the newspaper he expects the EBRD to help fund the $12 million reconstruction of the airport runway.
